To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have proposed a semantic model for event sources, which is based on the information provided in WSDL; (ii) we have proposed two metrics to evaluate event subscription accuracy; (iii) we have analyzed the accuracy of several existing event subscription strategies; (iv) we have proposed several design patterns for event brokers; (v) we have implemented a prototype to show that the design patterns are feasible.

we have proposed a conceptual model for Web service event sources based on WSDL, and we have proposed a set-theoretic subscription model for Web service events, and we have identified several event subscription strategies and analyzed the accuracy of these strategies.

we have proposed a semantic model for asynchronous event subscription, we have introduced two metrics to measure the accuracy and effectiveness of event subscription, we discussed the accuracy of several subscription strategies and the design patterns of Web service event broker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
modeling, analyzing and implementing event-based interactions in Web services.
modeling and analyzing the static and dynamic event subscription patterns in Web service interactions.
the semantic modeling and design patterns of Web service eventing.

the paper presents a conceptual model for static and dynamic events in WSDL, a set theoretic semantics for event subscriptions, two metrics for measuring the accuracy of event subscription, and four event broker design patterns based on two visibility and reachability factors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a semantic foundation for modeling event-based interactions and have discussed the impact of design patterns for asynchronous event-based interaction.
this paper presents a conceptual model for event modeling and event subscription, and proposes several design patterns for asynchronous event-based Web service interaction.

we provide a conceptual model for event sources and event sinks in Web service interaction and we propose a set of metrics to evaluate the accuracy of event subscription in a service interaction context.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the accuracy of event subscription is highly dependent on the event source and event sink visibility/reachability, and the broker design patterns can be used to improve the event subscription accuracy.
event subscription accuracy can be improved by using the event source information in WSDL and by applying event broker design patterns.
the event subscription standard proposals should be extended to include the visibility factor, and that the event broker should have a state to record the subscription and delivery information.
